topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Data Science students

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
lecture_lines: Imagine a magnifying glass sliding over data.
This filter captures local pixel patterns.
It slides, computes, and shifts sequentially.
animations: Fade in a rectangular window labeled 'Filter' with a icon at grid D3.
Slide the window containing across a grid of pixel data at D4.
Flash yellow #ffcc00 the interaction between window and pixels while displaying the icon.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics (The Sliding Dot Product)
lecture_lines: Multiply filter values by underlying pixels.
Sum these values into one new pixel.
This defines a single discrete convolution.
animations: Display the MathTex dot product formula: r'\\\\sum x_i \\\\cdot w_i' in #ffffff at B3.
Highlight the sliding window as a vector moving across pixel values in a grid at E2.
Show each pair (x_i * w_i) multiplication and update the total sum 'res' at E5.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Local Influence
lecture_lines: Each output pixel gathers local influence.
Spatial information flows into synthesized results.
animations: Fade in a 3x3 pixel region marked in #ffcc00 at C4.
Draw a box highlighting 3x3 neighbors of the influencing the output.
Animate a colored glow from the neighbor instances to the resulting pixel.

sections.title: Application: The Edge Detector
lecture_lines: The Sobel operator highlights intensity changes.
animations: Show a Sobel filter kernel with color #00ff00 at C3.
Slide the kernel over image at D3, updating intensity.

sections.title: Real-World Impact: Neural Networks
lecture_lines: CNNs learn these filter patterns automatically.
Edges form the foundation for features.
Filters stack to recognize complex objects.
animations: Visualize stacked convolution layers as a at B2 and C2.
Show pixel transition from raw grayscale to structural feature maps at B4 and C4.
Show stacked layers culminating in 'Result' and classification at B6 and C6.
